answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Agents log a per-identity pulse of request timing, tool mix, and error cadence, then cluster accounts whose patterns correlate too tightly across weeks. A cluster crossing the zenith of statistical similarity gets its shared payout frozen and its members re-verified, so each fake identity must sustain distinct, low-correlation activity it cannot cheaply fake. A lone raven account can mimic one honest peer, but holding hundreds apart long enough to escape clustering multiplies the attacker's compute and operational cost per identity.
